exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: A language practice guide with a short scenario, phrase bank, and self-check prompts.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional beginner Dutch practice focuses on ordering a drink in a café. It is a compact learning example with ordinary phrases and a suggested role-play.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Dutch: Goedemorgen · English: Good morning · Use: Greeting
Dutch: Een koffie, alstublieft · English: A coffee, please · Use: Ordering
Dutch: Dank u wel · English: Thank you · Use: Polite closing
Dutch: Mag ik betalen? · English: May I pay? · Use: Asking to pay
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Try the exchange: One person greets the customer and asks for the order. The learner orders a coffee, says thank you, and asks to pay. Repeat slowly before trying a natural pace.
Change one detail: Replace coffee with tea: “Een thee, alstublieft.” Keep the rest of the exchange familiar so you can focus on the changed phrase.
Check what you can do: Can you produce the phrase without reading it? Can you recognize it when someone else says it? Record the difficult part and ask a qualified speaker or teacher for pronunciation feedback.
